mainTopic: How a שומר must guard deposited money: the משנה's standard, רבי יצחק's teachings on money and ברכה, שמואל's burial rule, and cases of liability
overview: The משנה teaches that a שומר of deposited coins must guard them כדרך השומרים. If he ties them behind his back, gives them to young children, or locks them up poorly, he pays. The גמרא explains, from the פסוק 'וצרת הכסף בידך', that money must be kept in your hand and not behind you. It then brings teachings of רבי יצחק about money: keep cash on hand, split your wealth into thirds, and know that ברכה rests only on what is hidden from the eye. A ברייתא about praying before measuring grain backs up that idea. Next, שמואל rules that money is properly guarded only when buried. רבא adds limits around שבת, and the גמרא updates the hiding place as thieves change their methods. A burial depth of one טפח is enough, unlike the three טפחים needed for חמץ. The גמרא then tells three stories about שומרים. It rules that תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס is חייב, and that a שומר who says 'I don't know where I put it' must pay. The amud ends with רבא starting to analyze a case where the שומר gave the money to his mother, and the analysis continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: improper ways of guarding deposited coins
steps.stepSummary: A שומר who ties the coins and slings them behind him, gives them to his young children, or locks them up badly is חייב. If he guarded properly, he is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone deposits coins with a friend, and the friend ties them up and slings them over his back, or hands them to his young son or daughter, or locks them up in a way that isn't good enough, he must pay, because he didn't guard them the way guardians normally do. But if he guarded them the normal way, he does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three cases where a שומר of money guarded it badly, and rules that he must pay if it is lost or stolen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is כדרך השומרים, the normal standard that careful guardians use for money. Falling short of that standard counts as פשיעה (negligence), so the שומר is חייב. Meeting the standard makes him פטור even if the money is stolen anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: One who deposits an item with someone for safekeeping
He tied them up (in a cloth or bundle)
He slung them over his back
In the normal way that guardians guard
Liable to pay / exempt from paying

steps.whatToRemember: A שומר of money must meet the normal guarding standard. If he falls short, he pays.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who deposits coins with his fellow,
and [the fellow] tied them up and slung them behind his back,
or he handed them over to his young son or daughter,
or he locked [the door] in front of them in a way that wasn't proper,
he is liable, because he did not guard in the way guardians guard.
But if he guarded in the way guardians guard, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּפְקִיד מָעוֹת אֵצֶל חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר of money who ties it behind his back, gives it to minors, or locks it improperly is חייב for not guarding כדרך השומרים. If he guarded properly, he is פטור.

steps.title: What is wrong with tying the money and carrying it on his back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the other cases as clear negligence, but asks how tying the coins and slinging them behind him is a failure. What more could he have done?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that all the other cases count as not guarding properly. But when he tied up the money and slung it behind him, what else was he supposed to do?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges one case in the משנה: tying the money up and carrying it behind you seems like a careful way to guard it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving money to children and locking it badly are obviously poor guarding. But carrying the money on your own body seems like the most careful option there is. So why does the משנה call it negligence?

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
But (introducing the case that is hard)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Granted, all of [the other cases] are
[cases where] he did not guard in the way guardians guard.
But [where] he tied them up and slung them behind his back,
what [more] should he have done?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא כּוּלְּהוּ שֶׁלֹּא שִׁימֵּר כְּדֶרֶךְ הַשּׁוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one of the three cases listed in the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that tying the coins and slinging them behind him counts as negligence
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carrying the money on one's own body seems like maximum care, so it should not be called a failure to guard properly.

steps.title: The Torah requires money to be kept in your hand, in front of you
steps.stepSummary: רבא in the name of רבי יצחק learns from 'וצרת הכסף בידך' that even tied-up money must be kept in your hand, not behind you.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רבי יצחק: The פסוק says, 'And you shall tie up the money in your hand.' Even though the money is tied up, it must still be in your hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the proper way to guard money is in your hand, in front of you, where you can watch it. Behind your back is not good enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק adds 'בידך' after 'וצרת', which teaches that tying alone is not enough. The money must also be in your hand. Money behind your back can be taken without you noticing, so that is not כדרך השומרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (introducing a Torah source)

steps.whatToRemember: Money must be guarded in your hand, in front of you. Tied up behind your back counts as negligence.

phrases.english: Rava said in the name of Rabbi Yitzchak:
The verse says: "And you shall tie up the money in your hand,"

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁצְּרוּרִין – יִהְיוּ בְּיָדְךָ.
phrases.english: even though they are tied up, they must be in your hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source defining the guarding standard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tying the money and carrying it on your body seems like the best possible guarding.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah requires money to be kept in your hand. Behind your back falls below the standard, so the שומר is חייב.

steps.title: Always keep some money on hand
steps.stepSummary: Using the same פסוק, רבי יצחק teaches that a person should always have money available in his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: A person's money should always be available in his hand, as it says, 'And you shall tie up the money in your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the law of guarding to a piece of life advice from רבי יצחק, built on the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words 'בידך' that set the guarding standard are now read as general guidance: don't tie up all your money where you can't reach it. This begins a short series of teachings by רבי יצחק.

keyTerms.meaning: Always (introducing a piece of good advice)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא כַּסְפּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם מָצוּי בְּיָדוֹ,
phrases.english: A person's money should always be available in his hand,
as it is said: "And you shall tie up the money in your hand."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק לְעוֹלָם יְהֵא כַּסְפּוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק and the same author for practical advice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should always keep money readily available.

steps.title: Divide your money into three parts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק advises keeping a third of one's money in land, a third in business, and a third on hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: A person should always split his money into three: a third in land, a third in business, and a third in his own hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another money teaching from רבי יצחק: how to spread out your wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting money between land, trade, and cash means no single loss wipes everything out. The last third, 'תחת ידו', fits the previous teaching about always having money on hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Under his hand, kept on hand

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
A person should always divide his money into three:
a third in land, and a third in business,
and a third under his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק לְעוֹלָם יַשְׁלִישׁ אָדָם אֶת מְעוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רבי יצחק on managing money
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Divide wealth into thirds: land, business, and cash on hand.

steps.title: Blessing rests on what is hidden from the eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that ברכה is found only in something hidden from view, learning it from 'באסמיך' (in your storehouses).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Blessing is found only in something hidden from the eye, as it says, 'ה׳ will command the blessing with you in your storehouses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching of רבי יצחק: ברכה comes to things that are not on display or counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places the ברכה 'in your storehouses', where grain sits out of sight. From this רבי יצחק learns that ברכה rests on what is hidden. It loosely continues the theme of how to handle one's wealth.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אֵין הַבְּרָכָה מְצוּיָה
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said: Blessing is not found
except in something hidden from the eye,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יְצַו ה׳ אִתְּךָ אֶת הַבְּרָכָה בַּאֲסָמֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "ה׳ will command the blessing with you in your storehouses."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אֵין הַבְּרָכָה מְצוּיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further teaching of רבי יצחק connected to wealth
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכה rests only on what is hidden from the eye.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches the same idea
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that ברכה is found only in something the eye does not control, using the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Blessing is found only in something the eye has no control over, as it says, 'ה׳ will command the blessing with you in your storehouses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל that says almost the same thing as רבי יצחק, from the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is slightly different: 'שאין העין שולטת בו', meaning the eye has no power over it, instead of 'סמוי מן העין', hidden from the eye. This backs up רבי יצחק's teaching with an earlier תנאי source.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יצחק and דבי רבי ישמעאל learn from 'באסמיך' that ברכה rests on what is not exposed to the eye.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Blessing is not found except in something
that the eye has no control over,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יְצַו ה׳ אִתְּךָ אֶת הַבְּרָכָה בַּאֲסָמֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: as it is said: "ה׳ will command the blessing with you in your storehouses."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא supporting רבי יצחק's teaching
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכה rests only on what the eye does not control.

steps.title: A prayer for blessing before measuring grain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches what to say before and while measuring grain. A blessing said after measuring is a תפילת שוא, because ברכה rests only on what is hidden from the eye.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A person going to measure his grain says, 'May it be Your will that You send blessing in our work.' Once he starts measuring, he says, 'Blessed is He Who sends blessing into this pile.' If he already measured and only then prayed, his prayer is wasted. Blessing is not found in something weighed, measured, or counted. It is found only in something hidden from the eye, as the פסוק says, 'in your storehouses.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יצחק's teaching from step 6. Blessing only comes to something hidden from view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the grain is measured, its amount is still unknown, so it can still be blessed. Once it is measured, the amount is fixed and known, so praying for more is pointless. This ברייתא uses the same פסוק, 'באסמיך', that רבי יצחק used.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor, where the grain is piled
A prayer in vain, a useless prayer

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who goes to measure his threshing floor says:
"May it be Your will, ה׳ our God,
that You send blessing in the work of our hands."
If he began to measure, he says:
"Blessed is He Who sends blessing into this pile."
If he measured and only afterward said the blessing,
this is a prayer in vain,
because blessing is not found

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בְּדָבָר הַשָּׁקוּל וְלֹא בְּדָבָר הַמָּדוּד
phrases.english: not in something weighed and not in something measured
and not in something counted,
but only in something hidden from the eye,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יְצַו ה׳ אִתְּךָ אֶת הַבְּרָכָה בַּאֲסָמֶיךָ״.
phrases.english: as it says: "ה׳ will command the blessing with you in your storehouses."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַהוֹלֵךְ לָמוֹד אֶת גּוֹרְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 6 and 7 with a ברייתא that uses the same פסוק and the same idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pray for blessing before or during measuring, not after, because blessing rests only on what is hidden from the eye.

steps.title: Money is only guarded when buried
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the only proper way to guard money is to bury it in the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: Money is not properly guarded unless it is buried in the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new halachic rule from שמואל about how a שומר must guard money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money is small and easy to steal, so ordinary guarding is not enough. Burying it is the standard. A שומר who does less is treated as careless.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarding, the level of care a שומר owes

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
Money has no proper guarding
except in the ground.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic standard for the rest of the section. Every later step adjusts or explains this rule.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּסָפִים אֵין לָהֶם שְׁמִירָה אֶלָּא בַּקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the topic of blessing to the halacha of guarding money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money is properly guarded only when buried in the ground.

steps.title: No need to bury money right before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that שמואל agrees that money given at twilight on ערב שבת does not have to be buried right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: שמואל agrees that if someone receives money on ערב שבת at twilight, he does not have to bury it then. The רבנן did not burden him with that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds an exception to שמואל's rule. Right before שבת, you are not required to bury the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no time to dig and bury before שבת starts, so the רבנן did not demand it. The basic rule stays in place. It is just not enforced in this moment.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹדֵי שְׁמוּאֵל בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת,
phrases.english: And Shmuel agrees about Shabbat eve at twilight,
that the Rabbis did not burden him.
phrases.notes: If he got the money just before שבת, he does not have to bury it right then.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמוֹדֵי שְׁמוּאֵל בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits שמואל's rule in a time-pressure case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money received at twilight on ערב שבת need not be buried immediately.

steps.title: After שבת he must bury it, unless the owner may need it for הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: If he waits after שבת long enough to bury the money and does not, he is liable. If the owner is a צורבא מרבנן, the שומר may wait, thinking the owner might want coins for הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If after שבת he waited long enough to bury the money but did not, he is liable. But if the owner is a young Torah scholar, the שומר can think: maybe he will need the coins for הבדלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues רבא's exception and sets its limits. The grace period ends after שבת, except in the case of a צורבא מרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שבת exception lasts only until he has a chance to bury the money. Once that time passes, the regular rule applies again. A scholar is careful to make הבדלה, so the שומר may reasonably expect him to come back for coins to buy wine.

phrases.english: And if after Shabbat he waited
enough time to bury it and did not bury it,
he is liable.
And if he is a young Torah scholar,
phrases.notes: "He" is the owner of the money. The next line is what the שומר is thinking.

phrases.english: he thought: perhaps
he needs the coins for havdala.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי שְׁהָא לְמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת שִׁעוּר לְמִקְבְּרִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the end point of the שבת exception, and adds a further allowance for a scholar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Failing to bury after שבת makes him liable, unless the owner is a scholar who may need coins for הבדלה.

steps.title: When diggers are common, hide money in the roof beams
steps.stepSummary: Now that thieves dig for buried money, the safe place is in the roof beams.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nowadays, when diggers are common, money is properly guarded only in the roof beams.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא updates שמואל's rule because thieves have learned to dig. The ground is no longer safe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real standard is to hide money where thieves will not look. Burying was just the best way to do that in שמואל's time. When thieves change their methods, the hiding place changes too.

keyTerms.meaning: Diggers, thieves who probe for buried money

steps.confusionAlert: This does not reject שמואל. The principle is the same: hide it where thieves will not look. Only the practical place has changed.

phrases.english: And nowadays, when diggers are common,
phrases.notes: These are thieves who poke around in the ground to find buried money.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶן שְׁמִירָה אֶלָּא בִּשְׁמֵי קוֹרָה.
phrases.english: money is properly guarded only in the roof beams.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא דִּשְׁכִיחִי גָּשׁוֹשָׁאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Updates שמואל's hiding place for a later time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When diggers are common, money must be hidden in the roof beams.

steps.title: When beam-breakers are common, hide money between the bricks
steps.stepSummary: Now that thieves break into beams, the safe place is between the bricks of the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nowadays, when beam-breakers are common, money is properly guarded only between the bricks.
steps.whatsHappening: Thieves learned to search the beams, so the גמרא updates the hiding place again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the last step. A new method of stealing calls for a new hiding place, now inside the wall.

keyTerms.meaning: Breakers, thieves who tear open beams

phrases.english: And nowadays, when breakers are common,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶם שְׁמִירָה אֶלָּא בֵּינֵי אוּרְבֵי.
phrases.english: money is properly guarded only between the bricks.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא דִּשְׁכִיחִי פָּרוֹמָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further update after the roof beams also became unsafe.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When beam-breakers are common, money must be hidden between the bricks.

steps.title: שמואל agrees a wall or corners are also fine
steps.stepSummary: רבא says שמואל agrees that money hidden in a wall, or between the corners of the house, is properly guarded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: שמואל agrees that a wall is also good, or the space between the corners.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows that, even according to שמואל, burying in the ground is not the only acceptable option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said "only in the ground," but רבא explains that a wall or the corners are equally hidden. This shows the rule was about real hiding, not about the ground itself.

phrases.english: Rava said: And Shmuel agrees about a wall,
or also between the corners.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: וּמוֹדֶה שְׁמוּאֵל בְּכוֹתֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens שמואל's original rule to include the wall and corners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wall or the corners also count as proper guarding.

steps.title: When tappers are common, hide money near the floor or ceiling
steps.stepSummary: Now that thieves tap on walls to find hollow spots, money is safe only in the טפח of wall next to the floor or next to the ceiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nowadays, when tappers are common, money is properly guarded only in the handbreadth next to the ground, or the handbreadth next to the ceiling beams.
steps.whatsHappening: Thieves learned to tap on walls, so the גמרא gives the final update: hide the money at the very top or bottom of the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tapping does not reveal a hiding spot near the floor or ceiling, so those edges stay safe. This is the last stage in the chain of updates.

keyTerms.meaning: Tappers, thieves who knock on walls

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's rule really means hiding the money where thieves will not search. As thieves changed their methods, the place moved: ground, roof beams, between bricks, then near the floor or ceiling.

phrases.english: And nowadays, when tappers are common,
money is properly guarded
only in the handbreadth next to the ground,
or in the handbreadth next to the ceiling beams.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִידָּנָא דִּשְׁכִיחִי טָפוֹחָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final update in the chain of hiding places.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When tappers are common, hide money in the טפח next to the floor or the ceiling.

steps.title: Quoting the rule about חמץ buried under rubble
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב יוסף quotes a משנה: חמץ buried under rubble counts as destroyed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says this applies when a dog cannot sniff it out, which is three טפחים deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב יוסף said to רב אשי: There we learned that חמץ on which rubble fell is treated as destroyed. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: this applies whenever a dog cannot search it out. And it was taught: how deep can a dog search? Three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a question. It quotes a source about how deep something must be buried to count as gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This source gives a measure for burying: three טפחים is out of a dog's reach. The next step will ask whether burying money needs the same depth.

keyTerms.meaning: There we learned (in a משנה elsewhere)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Aha son of Rav Yosef said to Rav Ashi:
There we learned:
Chametz on which rubble fell
is as if it was destroyed.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין הַכֶּלֶב יָכוֹל לְחַפֵּשׂ אַחֲרָיו.
phrases.english: Any that a dog cannot search for.
And it was taught: How deep is a dog's search?
Three handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הָתָם תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source to set up a question about שמואל's burying rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Buried חמץ counts as destroyed when a dog cannot reach it, which is three טפחים.

steps.title: Must money be buried three טפחים deep?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא asks whether burying money also needs the three-טפחים depth, or whether less is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, what is the rule? Do we need three טפחים, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא asks his actual question: does שמואל's "bury it in the ground" require a depth of three טפחים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the measure used for חמץ also applies to guarding money. The two cases might be different, and רב אשי answers this in the next step.

phrases.english: Here, what is the rule?

phrases.aramaic: מִי בָּעֵינַן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: Do we require three handbreadths or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא מַאי? מִי בָּעֵינַן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the source from step 16 to שמואל's rule and asks the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether money must be buried three טפחים deep to count as properly guarded.

steps.title: Money needs less depth than חמץ because the reason is different
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that חמץ needs three טפחים because of smell, but money only needs to be hidden from sight, so three טפחים are not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, with חמץ, the concern is the smell, so we need three טפחים. Here, with money, the concern is only hiding it from people's eyes, so we do not need three טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אחא's question from step 17. Money does not need to be buried as deep as חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-טפחים rule for חמץ exists because a dog can smell bread and dig it up. Money has no smell. The only danger is that a person will see it, so the depth needed is set by a different reason.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches a basic method: a measurement from one area of הלכה carries over only if the reason behind it also carries over.

phrases.english: He said to him: There, because of the scent,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the חמץ case from step 16. 'He' is רב אשי, answering רב אחא's question.

phrases.english: we require three handbreadths.
Here, because it is about hiding it from the eye,
we do not require three handbreadths.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם מִשּׁוּם רֵיחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Money does not need three טפחים, because the concern is sight, not smell.

steps.title: So how deep must the money be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the required depth is, if not three טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If money doesn't need three טפחים, how deep does it need to be? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 only said what is NOT needed. This short question asks for the actual minimum depth.

phrases.english: And how much?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follow-up to step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum depth for burying deposited money

steps.title: One טפח is enough
steps.stepSummary: רפרם מסיכרא rules that money must be buried one טפח deep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רפרם from Sikhera said: one טפח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: burying money one טפח deep counts as proper guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One טפח is enough to hide the money from sight. That is all that is needed, since smell is not an issue.

keyTerms.meaning: רפרם from the town of Sikhera

steps.whatToRemember: To guard deposited money by burying it, one טפח deep is enough. חמץ needs three טפחים because of a dog's sense of smell.

phrases.english: Rafram from Sikhera said: A handbreadth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַפְרָם מִסִּיכְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19

steps.title: Story: money kept in a willow hut was stolen
steps.stepSummary: A שומר put deposited money in a hut made of willow branches, and it was stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man deposited money with his friend. The friend put it in a hut made of willow branches, and it was stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a שומר. This step only lays out the facts and sets up רב יוסף's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question will be whether keeping money in a flimsy willow hut counts as proper guarding. The money was stolen, not burned.

keyTerms.meaning: A hut made of willow branches

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַפְקֵיד זוּזֵי גַּבֵּי חַבְרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: A certain man deposited money with his friend;
he placed it in a hut of willow branches;
it was stolen.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַפְקֵיד זוּזֵי גַּבֵּי חַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case about guarding money
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: money in a willow hut was stolen.

steps.title: רב יוסף: negligence at the start, accident at the end, so he is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the hut was safe from thieves but negligent regarding fire. That makes the case תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס, and the שומר is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: even though the hut is good guarding against thieves, it is negligence regarding fire. So this is a case that started with negligence and ended with an accident, and he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rules on the willow-hut case. He holds the שומר liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hut protected well against theft, so the theft itself was an אונס. But putting money in a hut that could easily burn was negligent from the start. רב יוסף holds that a loss which began with פשיעה, even if it ended through אונס, makes the שומר pay.

keyTerms.meaning: It started with negligence and ended with an unavoidable accident

steps.confusionAlert: The money was not lost by fire. It was stolen, and against thieves the hut was fine. The negligence was about a different danger, fire. That is exactly why the case is called 'negligence at the start, accident at the end.'

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְעִנְיַן גַּנָּבֵי – נְטִירוּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Even though with regard to thieves it is proper guarding,
with regard to fire it is negligence;
so it is a case of negligence at the start and accident at the end,
he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְעִנְיַן גַּנָּבֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case of step 21
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Negligent regarding fire, safe regarding thieves: started with פשיעה, ended with אונס, so the שומר is חייב.

steps.title: Other version of רב יוסף: he is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב יוסף's ruling the other way: the start was negligent, the end was an accident, and the שומר is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: even though regarding fire it is negligence, regarding thieves it is proper guarding. It started with negligence and ended with an accident, so he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב יוסף's ruling. In this version the שומר is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The facts are the same: negligent toward fire, safe toward thieves. The two versions disagree about the rule. This version holds that if the actual loss came from an אונס, the earlier negligence does not make him pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the statement)

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְעִנְיַן נוּרָא – פְּשִׁיעוּתָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Even though with regard to fire it is negligence,
with regard to thieves it is proper guarding;
and negligence at the start and accident at the end is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אַף עַל גַּב דִּלְעִנְיַן נוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Alternative version of step 22 with the opposite outcome
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס is פטור.

steps.title: The הלכה: negligence at the start makes him liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that when a loss began with negligence and ended with an accident, the שומר is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: negligence at the start and accident at the end, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the dispute between the two versions. The first version is the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the two versions gave opposite rulings, the גמרא decides in favor of liability. In the willow-hut case, the שומר must pay.
steps.whatToRemember: תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס is חייב. A שומר who was negligent at the start pays, even if the loss itself came through an accident.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key rule in the laws of שומרים. Negligence about one danger can make a שומר liable for a loss caused by a different danger.

phrases.english: And the halakha is:
negligence at the start and accident at the end, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִילְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between steps 22 and 23
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תחילתו בפשיעה וסופו באונס is חייב.

steps.title: Story: the שומר doesn't know where he put the money
steps.stepSummary: An owner asks for his deposited money back, and the שומר says he doesn't know where he put it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man deposited money with his friend. He said to him: give me my money! The friend said: I don't know where I put it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a שומר. This step gives the facts and sets up רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שומר does not claim it was stolen or lost through an accident. He simply cannot find it. The question is whether that counts as negligence.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַפְקֵיד זוּזֵי גַּבֵּי חַבְרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: A certain man deposited money with his friend;
he said to him: Give me my money!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא יָדַעְנָא הֵיכָא אוֹתְבִינְהוּ.
phrases.english: He said to him: I don't know where I put it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַפְקֵיד זוּזֵי גַּבֵּי חַבְרֵיהּ, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַב לִי זוּזַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case about a שומר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: the שומר cannot say where he put the money.

steps.title: רבא: 'I don't know' is negligence, so go pay
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that any 'I don't know' claim from a שומר is itself negligence, and he must pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבא. He said to him: every 'I don't know' is negligence. Go pay.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules on the 'I don't know' case. The שומר must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A proper שומר knows where he put the deposit. Not knowing shows he did not guard it properly, so no further proof of negligence is needed.
steps.whatToRemember: A שומר who says 'I don't know where I put it' is treated as negligent and must pay.

phrases.english: It came before Rava; he said to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is speaking to the שומר, the one who said 'I don't know.'

phrases.english: Every 'I don't know' is negligence;
go pay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the case of step 25
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'I don't know where I put it' is itself פשיעה, so the שומר pays.

steps.title: Story: the שומר gave the money to his mother
steps.stepSummary: A שומר handed deposited money to his mother. She put it in a chest, and it was stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man deposited money with his friend. The friend gave it to his mother, she put it in a chest, and it was stolen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a third story about a שומר. This step lays out the facts and sets up רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case adds a new twist: the שומר passed the money to someone else, his mother. She stored it in a chest, and it was stolen from there.

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַפְקֵיד זוּזֵי גַּבֵּי חַבְרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: A certain man deposited money with his friend;
he handed it over to his mother,
and she put it in a chest, and it was stolen.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּאַפְקֵיד זוּזֵי גַּבֵּי חַבְרֵיהּ, אַשְׁלְמִינְהוּ לְאִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case about a שומר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets out the facts: the money was given to the שומר's mother, put in a chest, and stolen.

steps.title: רבא asks how judges should rule in this case
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises the question of how judges can decide the case of the mother and the chest.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: how should judges rule in this case?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens the discussion of the mother case with a question. This is a setup line; his analysis comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's wording suggests the case is not simple. Each possible party (the שומר or his mother) may have a claim that frees them, and the next lines will explore this.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הֵיכִי נְדַיְינוּ דַּיָּינֵי לְהַאי דִּינָא?
phrases.english: Rava said: How should judges judge this case?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֵיכִי נְדַיְינוּ דַּיָּינֵי לְהַאי דִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the analysis of the case in step 27
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who, if anyone, is liable when the שומר gave the money to his mother and it was stolen from her chest

steps.title: Should the שומר himself be told to pay?
steps.stepSummary: רבא tries out the first option, telling the שומר to pay, and begins to show that the שומר can push back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say to him, the שומר: Go pay! But he can say:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is working through his question by testing the first answer: make the son, the שומר, pay. This line sets up the next move, the שומר's defense, which the גמרא gives right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28, רבא asked how the judges can decide this case. Now he tests one side: maybe the שומר should pay, since he handed the money to someone else. The word אָמַר signals that the שומר has a claim that blocks this ruling, so this option is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say. Introduces a suggestion that is being tested.
To him himself, meaning the שומר and not his mother.

phrases.english: Let us say to him himself:
phrases.notes: "Him himself" is the son, the שומר who gave the money to his mother.

phrases.english: Go pay!
But he can say:
phrases.notes: The שומר is about to defend himself. His actual argument comes in the very next line.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא לֵיהּ לְדִידֵיהּ זִיל שַׁלֵּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's question from step 28 by testing the first possible ruling: making the שומר pay.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the judges make the שומר (the son) pay for the stolen deposit, or does he have a valid defense?
